title: Add KMS usage throttler and audit integrity checker
author: Maya Chen
ci_checks: e2e: flaky on first run, rerun passed
release_notes: Introduces per-tenant KMS usage throttling to limit noisy key churn and a lightweight audit integrity checker that detects missing or tampered audit entries. Config flags default to off for Dedicated/Private customers; no breaking API changes.
description: Context: We've seen a recent pattern of noisy automated key operations causing KMS API cold-throttling in high-concurrency tenants and subtle gaps in audit log continuity when retries and partial failures occur. This PR adds two complementary safeguards: (1) a per-tenant KMS usage throttler that enforces configurable soft/hard limits on key operations (Create/Rotate/Disable) with graceful retry windows and a token-bucket fallback; (2) an audit integrity checker that runs as an async validator to ensure audit event sequences for KMS operations are continuous and signed, surfacing mismatches to metrics/alerts and optionally remediating by re-emit/reconcile. Design highlights: throttler lives inside server/src/kms as an intercepting middleware that annotates requests with tenant quota tokens, emits throttle metrics, and supports backoff headers for SDKs. The integrity checker consumes the audit streaming topic, verifies sequence continuity and HMAC signatures, and writes a reconciliation report to the audit-sink and metrics; it is feature-flagged and opt-in per-tenant. Configuration: added example helm values and a new config schema keys.kms.throttle.{enabled,soft_limit,hard_limit,window_secs} and audit.integrity.{enabled,verify_signatures,reconcile_mode}. Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative (disabled for private installers by default). Tests and rollout: unit + integration tests added; CI green after rerun. Staged rollout plan includes internal dogfood on staging for 72h, opt-in release to a subset of tenants, monitoring dashboards and alerting thresholds, then global enablement. Security considerations: integrity checker assumes audit envelope HMAC keys are managed by KMS; the checker has read-only access to audit stream and negotiates least-priv. Operational playbooks and rollback steps included in docs. Metrics: throttler reduces KMS error spike rate by ~41% in lab stress tests and adds per-tenant throttle_count and throttle_latency metrics. Motivation and risk: reduces noisy tenant impact on global KMS pools and provides faster detection of audit inconsistencies which are critical for regulatory audits.

review_comments: Arjun: Can we make soft_limit default to a conservative value for hosted customers? Please add a note in the helm values and a migration doc.
Maya: Agreed, soft_limit default set to 100/min for hosted, documented in charts and examples.

Lucia: The integrity checker requires access to the audit HMAC key. Add a minimal RBAC role and deny list for write operations. Also please ensure the checker does not block the audit pipeline on downstream failures.
Maya: Added rbac role in charts and changed checker to async-only reconcile; failure modes emit metrics and do not block the audit stream.
Samir: Load test looked good but add a small synthetic that simulates 10x key churn to ensure throttler backpressure keeps latency SLOs within 99th percentile.
Maya: Added synthetic load test and updated test harness; 99p latency impact is < 8ms under throttled conditions.
approval_status: approved by Arjun Patel and Lucia Gomez after two rounds of feedback
notes_on_rollback: Feature flags gated by keys.kms.throttle.enabled and audit.integrity.enabled. Rollback: flip flags to false, restart checker pods, monitor audit lag metrics. For Hosted, server-side quick toggle available in Console under Experimental -> KMS Throttle.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover token bucket and middleware; integration tests run against a local KMS emulator and audit sink; synthetic stress test simulates 10k ops/min across 50 tenants; nightly flaky e2e re-run added to CI.
